criteria.criterion: Access the RFC Editor record for RFC 9110 (info page) and base answers on it
criteria.description: Navigate to the RFC Editor info page/record for RFC 9110 (e.g., rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110) and use it as the source. Full credit if the agent attempts to access the RFC Editor record and clearly reports being blocked/unable to load the page (e.g., downtime, captcha, network error). Partial credit if the agent uses another source without clearly indicating the RFC Editor record was inaccessible.

criteria.criterion: Report RFC 9110 core metadata from the RFC Editor record

Full credit only if all four are present and match the RFC Editor record. Partial credit if one element is missing/incorrect. If the RFC Editor record is not accessible and the agent clearly states that, do not award zero automatically; award partial credit if the agent correctly explains the limitation and does not fabricate data.

Full credit if correct for every item. Partial credit if correct for some but not all, or if the agent lists the RFCs but omits the full/partial labels. If the RFC Editor record is inaccessible and the agent clearly states that, award partial credit for not hallucinating the full/partial distinction.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:

The rubric criterion assessed: correct extraction of RFC 9110 metadata (title, publication month/year, status, authors) and RFC Editor-recorded obsolescence relationships including full vs partial.

Supported by DOM: title ("RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics"), status ("Internet Standard"), and authors ("R. Fielding , Ed.", "M. Nottingham , Ed.", "J. Reschke , Ed.") are explicitly present in DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0. Obsolescence relationships are partially supported: the Abstract explicitly lists obsoleted RFCs (2818, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694) and explicitly marks RFC 7230 as only partially obsoleted via the phrase "portions of 7230." However, the DOM snapshot does not show the publication month and year; therefore that required metadata cannot be verified from the provided DOM state. Additionally, while the abstract supports partial vs full for 7230 vs the others, the snapshot does not show the RFC Editor "Obsoletes" field in the "About this RFC" tab, so confirmation that these relationships are coming from the RFC Editor record fields (as opposed to only the document text) is incomplete in the DOM evidence provided.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent answer claims publication date "June 2022" and status details "also designated STD 97"; STD 97 is visible in DOM ("RFC 9110 STD 97: HTTP Semantics"), but "June 2022" is not present in DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0. The agent answer also asserts an "Obsoletes (9)" list and provides per-RFC titles and a "Details" section under "About this RFC"; none of that list/detail section text is visible in the provided DOM snapshot because "About this RFC" is selected=false in DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0. Therefore, the DOM evidence supports the abstract’s obsoletes sentence (including partial obsolescence of RFC 7230) but does not support the claimed month/year or the existence/content of an "Obsoletes (9)" field in the record view within this snapshot.
